issues.problem: Session order deadlocks the bundle. S1 moves docs/playbook.md and makes bundle args refuse a missing explicitly configured playbook, but the migration that drops the stale config key lands only in S2.
issues.suggested_fix: Implement in-memory migration before moving the playbook, combine both in S1, or keep a temporary compatibility symlink through S2. Add a dogfood assertion that S1's checkout can emit S2's workflow args.
issues.failure_scenario: After S1, cookwright.json v1 still has paths.playbook 'docs/playbook.md' but the file moved; 'bundle args stage-3 implement:s2' refuses, so the workflow needed to implement the migration cannot launch.
issues.evidence: Resolved by disposition 13 and §4.1: s1's move commit drops paths.playbook from this repo's cookwright.json, so absent means node_modules/cookwright/docs/playbook.md through the workspace link (node_modules/cookwright -> ../packages/cookwright, verified). The s1 checkpoint in §10 measures 'bundle args stage-3 implement:s2' on this repo, and §7.1 now expects only the version bump.

issues.problem: Pointer classification is destructive and contradictory: unknown dangling symlinks are replaced as 'earlier pointer' while unknown resolving symlinks are treated as user-owned. This repo's legacy in-repo pointers resolve after S1, so the table keeps them while §7 requires updating them to node_modules.
issues.suggested_fix: Enumerate recognized current and legacy cookwright target texts and update those regardless of resolution; preserve every unknown link including dangling ones. Replace links atomically. Test a known resolving legacy link and an unknown dangling user link.
issues.failure_scenario: Init deletes a user's temporarily dangling skill link and replaces it; conversely this repo's legacy links stay unchanged, so S6's expected 'updated' rows and 17-PASS doctor result fail.
issues.evidence: Resolved by disposition 14 and the §4.4 table: ownership is decided by link text ('text first, resolution never deciding ownership'), with past forms in POINTER_TEXTS_PAST and every other link, dangling or resolving, 'skipped'. s1 writes this repo's links in the final node_modules form, so §7.2 now expects 'kept'. §6 tests an injected past form ('updated') and a user's dangling link ('skipped', byte-identical).

issues.problem: Proposed hook commands interpolate the config-relative path inside double-quoted shell text without escaping.
issues.suggested_fix: Quote the relative path as a shell word (existing shellWord approach). Test spaces, single quotes, $(), backticks and semicolons for both host commands.
issues.failure_scenario: A config directory such as apps/$(command) causes command substitution on every SessionStart; spaces or quotes make the hook cd to the wrong directory.
issues.evidence: Resolved by dispositions 15 and 16 and §4.4: the hookCommand(rel) change is withdrawn. Claude's hook command is unchanged, and Codex's command uses cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel ...)" with 'no path is interpolated'. Disposition 15 records shellWord quoting for the bundle that does interpolate.

issues.problem: Plan wrongly claims to narrow B-002. Appending the top-to-config relative path to CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR does not fix sessions started below a top-level config and can double the path when the project dir is already the nested config root. Both host commands still look for node_modules only after entering the config root. Git shims in src/lib/hooks/shims.mjs are unchanged and cannot use a package hoisted to the work-tree top.
issues.suggested_fix: Resolve config root and installed package independently at runtime (config root and work-tree top). Update hooks/shims.mjs and tests; run hook tests with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR at top, config root and another subdirectory. Do not narrow B-002 until these pass.
issues.failure_scenario: With cookwright.json under apps/mobile and cookwright hoisted at the top, SessionStart and git hooks print 'package not installed' and exit cleanly; secret scan, doc sync, push gate and changelog verify never run though top-hoisted installs are claimed supported.
issues.evidence: Resolved by dispositions 6 and 16, §3 Out and §9: the B-002 claim is withdrawn, the hook commands and shims stay as stage 2 left them, and B-002 stays open. Its text gains a note that the pointers handle a top-hoisted package and the hooks and shims do not, and §9(f) opens the hoisted-hook work. One residual is only wording: §9 lists B-002 under 'narrowed', while disposition 6 says 'not narrowed'.

issues.problem: Path base for a top-hoisted package is undefined. installedPackage(repo) returns a root-relative path, but a package at the work-tree top is outside a nested config root; pointer() resolves against repo.root while the workflow pointer lives at the work-tree top.
issues.suggested_fix: Pick one explicit base (config root or work-tree top) for every workflow path, keep both roots in repo context, convert plan/state/rules/playbook/script paths consistently. Add an end-to-end nested-config/top-hoisted bundle status and bundle args test.
issues.failure_scenario: For apps/mobile/cookwright.json with top-level node_modules/cookwright, bundle args hashes the wrong file, emits a '..' path resolved from the wrong cwd, or prints an unresolvable script path.
issues.evidence: Resolved by disposition 17 and §4.1: every path printed or hashed is relative to the config root, and a hoisted package yields ../../node_modules/cookwright/... hashed from the config root. status prints the named Workflow form, so no script path is resolved. §6 bundle tests cover a nested config root with the package hoisted, for both args and status.

issues.problem: Setup procedure is not a verification loop and QA bypasses its main behavior: only the first doctor run is unconditional, remedies do not rerun doctor, and QA runs migrate and init manually before invoking /setup.
issues.suggested_fix: Specify doctor -> remedy -> doctor again until complete or blocked. In QA invoke /setup on the initial migrated/stale/missing-pointer readout and let it drive migrate and init; assert actions and final doctor output.
issues.failure_scenario: The skill acts on stale diagnoses, misses output produced by migration, or stops without proving completion; QA passes even if the skill cannot remediate any WARN/FAIL.
issues.evidence: Resolved by disposition 18, §4.5 ('The procedure is a loop': doctor, one remedy, doctor again until complete or a chosen state; 'never act on a readout older than the last remedy') and the §8 QA leg (run /setup on the initial three-line readout and let it drive migrate, init and the doctor rerun to complete, with the actions and final readout recorded).

issues.problem: The 'each non-PASS line' recipe is incomplete and sometimes host-wrong: no coverage of invalid/non-integer config versions, user-owned pointer conflicts, linked pointer parents, other pointer WARN states; 'host.rules shadowed -> README import paragraph' is a Claude remedy, not for Codex AGENTS.override.md.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the recipe exhaustive by check, status/subreason and host, with explicit 'chosen state; explain and stop' outcomes and remediation or escalation for every emitted doctor variant.
issues.failure_scenario: A Codex repo with AGENTS.override.md is told to add a Claude @AGENTS.md import which cannot clear the warning; other non-PASS states get no action.
issues.evidence: Partly resolved. §4.5 now splits host.rules into Claude shadowed and Codex override, the latter a chosen state, and covers config invalid and newer and the user's own pointers. But the table it calls 'exhaustive by check, status and host' still has no entry for several variants doctor emits today. rules.block WARN newer ('block vN is newer than this cookwright (update cookwright)', rules.mjs:26) and FAIL malformed (rules.mjs:30) are missing, since only 'stale or absent' is listed. host.rules FAIL old Claude version (claude.mjs:50) is missing. host.hook FAIL invalid JSON (claude.mjs:77) is missing, and init would not fix it. git WARN baseBranch missing (basics.mjs:27) is missing, since only git FAIL is listed. Two new variants are not named either: the Codex host.hook wrong-matcher WARN and host.pointers 'not required at level 0'. The loop applies 'exactly one remedy from the recipe table to the first line that is not PASS', so these lines get no defined action.

issues.problem: Ignored pointers are only annotated, not made persistent; the ignore probe cannot establish the source is a 'global ignore'; plain git add rejects an ignored pointer.
issues.suggested_fix: Report only 'ignored by git' unless source is measured. Treat an untracked ignored required pointer as weak/failing, give a consented 'git add -f <named paths>' remedy or other placement, and test the fresh-clone result.
issues.failure_scenario: Doctor passes locally because the pointer exists but it was never committed; a fresh clone lacks skill and workflow pointers and the documented 'git add <paths>' fails.
issues.evidence: Resolved by disposition 19, §4.4 and §4.5. The init note says only 'ignored by git'. Doctor reads an ours, untracked, ignored pointer as WARN 'ignored by git; git add -f <path> to track it'. The setup recipe maps it to 'git add -f <the named path>' with consent. §6 tests the doctor WARN naming git add -f.

issues.problem: Only a symlink at the immediate pointer directory is handled, not a symlink in an earlier path component; this is the invariant enforced by linkOnPath/refuseLinks.
issues.suggested_fix: Detect any linked component in the pointer's parent path and return a skipped row; exempt only the final pointer from refuseLinks. Test .claude and .claude/skills as links and prove the external target is untouched.
issues.failure_scenario: If .claude is a symlink but .claude/skills resolves as a normal dir, pointer code may write outside the repo; if refuseLinks stays unchanged, the whole init refuses instead of skipping just the pointer row.
issues.evidence: Resolved by disposition 19 and the §4.4 table row 'a symlinked component anywhere on the pointer's parent path -> skipped (never a whole-run refusal)'. refuseLinks 'exempts the final pointer only', and §6 tests '.claude or .claude/skills itself a link -> the rows skipped, the external target untouched, the other steps unaffected'.

issues.problem: Graceful handling of filesystems refusing symlinks conflicts with the planned doctor verdict: init continues but doctor reports the missing pointer as FAIL on non-Windows.
issues.suggested_fix: Define a durable way to distinguish unsupported symlinks from ordinary drift, or narrow the support claim and backlog it. Test final init exit code and subsequent doctor behavior.
issues.failure_scenario: On a filesystem without symlink support, init does other writes then exits nonzero because doctor sees drift the user cannot clear; later doctor runs keep failing, violating 'every piece optional'.
issues.evidence: Half resolved. Disposition 19 and §4.4 narrow the claim ('a non-Windows filesystem refusing links is not supported in this stage and doctor reports the missing pointer as FAIL there'), which removes the contradiction. The second half of the fix, backlogging it, is not done: §9's opened list (a) covers Windows only, and the plan says 'only Windows is backlogged'. So a known permanent FAIL the user cannot clear (a non-Windows filesystem without symlink support, such as exFAT or some network mounts) has no stable backlog id, which the AGENTS.md backlog discipline requires for an out-of-scope discovery.

issues.problem: Codex hook detection is command-only though the matcher matters; init merges only when the command is absent and doctor passes when the file 'carries the doctor hook'.
issues.suggested_fix: Treat command plus required matcher as one hook identity; WARN/update on wrong or incomplete matcher. Test missing, wrong, narrower and equivalent matchers.
issues.failure_scenario: Same command under a matcher covering startup but not resume (or an unrelated event): init keeps it, doctor PASSes, resumed sessions never run doctor.
issues.evidence: Resolved by disposition 21 and §4.4. hostfile.mjs identifies a hook by command and matcher, and a hook with the command and a wrong matcher is 'updated'. Doctor gives PASS on command and matcher, WARN on the command with another matcher, FAIL when absent. §6 tests 'updated on the command with another matcher' and doctor's wrong matcher -> WARN.

issues.problem: Codex rules check looks only for AGENTS.override.md beside root AGENTS.md, contradicting the stated directory-walk behavior; a nearer override between invocation dir and root is ignored.
issues.suggested_fix: Scan from invocation directory through the config/work-tree root for override files, report root-relative names, and test a nested invocation directory.
issues.failure_scenario: apps/mobile/AGENTS.override.md overrides root instructions for a session started there while doctor reports host.rules PASS.
issues.evidence: The check is fixed, but the session-start readout still misses the case. Disposition 21 and §4.4 make the Codex rules check walk 'from the invocation directory up through the root' with shadowingFiles, and §6 tests a nested invocation directory. However, §4.4's Codex hookCommand starts with cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || echo .)" before running doctor. Doctor's invocation cwd at SessionStart is therefore always the work-tree top, never the session's cwd (Codex runs hooks in the session cwd). For a session started in apps/mobile with apps/mobile/AGENTS.override.md, the session-start doctor line walks only from the top and still reports host.rules PASS, which is the original failure scenario. Only a by-hand doctor run from apps/mobile catches it.

issues.problem: Scope for --base on an existing config is unresolved: §4.2 says refuse it, but tests and S4 scope cover only --hosts, and §9 conditionally backlogs --base.
issues.suggested_fix: Decide now: include --base refusal in S4 with a test, or remove it from §4 and open a stable backlog item. Remove the 'if not folded in' wording.
issues.failure_scenario: Implementation follows session scope, leaving --base silently ignored while the plan/closeout claim §4 done; or an implementer fixes it outside the declared surface.
issues.evidence: Resolved by disposition 22, §4.2 ('--hosts and --base are refused ... in s4 with tests'), §6 ('--hosts and --base with an existing config -> refused'), §5 (src/init.mjs 'the two existing-config refusals') and §10 s4 ('--hosts and the two existing-config refusals'). The conditional §9 line is gone.

issues.location: Scope line 39; state homes lines 150-152; split lines 165-167
issues.problem: Plan closes E-014 before its implementation session and declares the CI session (S7) 'droppable if the bundle runs long'; S5 owns backlog updates while S7 builds the fixture; 'runs long' is untestable and state already has a mandatory S7 phase.
issues.suggested_fix: Make S7 mandatory, or formally revise plan/split and leave E-014 open before skipping. Close each backlog item only when its implementation and verification complete.
issues.failure_scenario: E-014 recorded closed with no fixture or workflow, or S7 becomes a no-op while scope and verification still claim §4.7 shipped.
issues.evidence: Resolved by disposition 22, §10 ('seven sessions, sequential, all mandatory'; a scope cut is a formal plan revision), §3 and §9 (E-014 narrowed, not closed), and s7 owning 'E-014's narrowed line'.

issues.problem: The create-expo-app measurement is not reproducible: the inspected npm/npx cache contains 5.0.0, not 5.0.1.
issues.suggested_fix: Remeasure the exact published tarball/version before implementation, record the command and generated files, and pin the verified value; drop '5.0.1 in the npx cache' unless demonstrated.
issues.failure_scenario: S7 pins an unmeasured/unavailable version; the fixture fails before testing cookwright or exercises a different scaffold than described.
issues.evidence: Resolved by disposition 22 and §4.7: 's7 measures the exact published version from the registry and the files the scaffold writes before pinning ... so nothing is claimed here'. The 5.0.1 claim is gone from the intro and §4.7, and §8 records the measured version in s7's report.

issues.location: Files inventory line 111; §4.3 line 59; S2 line 162
issues.problem: Changed-file inventory omits packages/cookwright/src/lib/doctor/basics.mjs, where checkConfig unconditionally returns PASS when config loaded; it must change to emit the migration WARN. If B-002 is fixed, src/lib/hooks/shims.mjs is also missing.
issues.suggested_fix: Add src/lib/doctor/basics.mjs and its tests to S2 and the file list; if B-002 is fixed, add src/lib/hooks/shims.mjs to the declared surface.
issues.failure_scenario: Implementer follows the inventory and migrated v1 configs keep reporting PASS, or touches an undeclared file creating a scope discrepancy in review.
issues.evidence: Resolved by disposition 24, §5 Changed (src/lib/doctor/{registry,claude,basics}.mjs), §4.3 (checkConfig in doctor/basics.mjs gives the WARN) and §10 s2 (doctor's config WARN in basics.mjs). shims.mjs is not needed, since B-002 is not fixed (disposition 16).

issues.problem: s1 moves docs/playbook.md and adds the refusal for a configured playbook that is missing. It never touches this repo's own `paths.playbook: "docs/playbook.md"` (cookwright.json:11). §7.1 counts on that stale key surviving until s6's migrate. The only thing that would neutralise the key is the in-memory 1->2 migration, and that lands in s2, which needs `bundle args` to launch.
issues.suggested_fix: In s1's move commit, drop `paths.playbook` from this repo's cookwright.json, since the key is optional from s1 on and absent means node_modules/cookwright/docs/playbook.md through the workspace link. Add it to s1's scope and checkpoint ('bundle args through the node_modules link' measured on this repo). Restate §7.1 so it expects only the version bump and the relaid note. A plain v1 file is the migration case the tests already cover.
issues.failure_scenario: After implement:s1 commits the move, the orchestrator runs `bundle phase stage-3 start implement:s2` and then `bundle args stage-3 implement:s2`. workflowArgs calls playbookPath(config), gets 'docs/playbook.md', finds it missing and exits 2 with s1's own refusal ('the playbook is not at docs/playbook.md (paths.playbook names it)'). Under disposition 4, `bundle status` refuses too. The bundle halts after its first session, and the only way forward is a hand edit of a code file outside any session.
issues.evidence: Resolved exactly as suggested: disposition 13, §4.1 ('paths.playbook dropped from this repo's cookwright.json' in the move commit), §10 s1 (in scope, with 'bundle args stage-3 implement:s2 measured on this repo' as a checkpoint) and §7.1 restated ('paths.playbook was dropped in s1').

issues.location: §4.1 (s1 rewrites the three tracked links) vs §4.4 row table vs §7.2/§7.3
issues.problem: s1 rewrites .claude/skills/bundle and the two workflow links to in-repo targets (../../packages/cookwright/...). These links resolve and their text is not one of the two forms §4.4 calls ours. By the plan's own row table, a link of other text that resolves is `skipped  your own link; cookwright's <name> is not reachable`, and doctor reports it as WARN. §7.2 instead expects these three rows to read `updated`, and §7.3 expects 17 PASS. s6's checkpoint 'dogfood committed with doctor 17 PASS' cannot be reached as the plan is written.
issues.suggested_fix: Have s1 write the three links straight in the form init will produce (../../node_modules/cookwright/skills/bundle and ../../node_modules/cookwright/hosts/claude/workflows/<name>.js). These resolve today through node_modules/cookwright -> ../packages/cookwright (measured). s6's init then reads `kept` for them and `wrote` only for setup. Restate §7.2 to match.
issues.failure_scenario: In s6: `npx cookwright init` prints `skipped .claude/skills/bundle your own link; cookwright's bundle is not reachable` and the same for bundle-phase.js and docs-audit.js. `npx cookwright doctor` then shows host.pointers WARN naming three links of 'yours', so the readout is '16 PASS, 1 WARN', not '17 PASS'. The implementer either hand-deletes the links (out of the plan) or cannot meet the checkpoint.
issues.evidence: Resolved as suggested: §4.1 rewrites the links 'in their final form' (../../node_modules/cookwright/skills/bundle and ../../node_modules/cookwright/hosts/claude/workflows/<name>.js), which matches the §4.4 'ours' pattern. §7.2 now expects 'kept' for the three and 'wrote' for setup, and §7.3 expects 17 PASS. node_modules/cookwright -> ../packages/cookwright verified on disk.

issues.location: §2 disposition 5, §4.4 row table ('a symlink of other text that resolves to nothing -> updated earlier pointer replaced')
issues.problem: Any dangling link of other text at .claude/skills/<name> or .agents/skills/<name> is classed as 'an earlier pointer'. No cookwright release has ever written a pointer (stages 1-2 wrote none), so for now every link this rule replaces belongs to the user. Doctor turns it into a FAIL 'run init', and init then deletes the user's link. Rule 2 says a state the user chose is a WARN, not drift that init overwrites.
issues.suggested_fix: Recognise an earlier pointer by text, the way hookCommandsPast does. Keep a POINTER_TEXTS_PAST list, empty in this stage, or match the shape `(../)*[<rel>/]node_modules/cookwright/(skills|hosts/<host>/workflows)/<name>`. Treat any other dangling link as the user's: `skipped`, WARN naming it. Add a test where a user's dangling link of another shape is left byte-identical.
issues.failure_scenario: A user keeps `.claude/skills/setup -> ../../../dotfiles/skills/setup`, a personal skill whose target is missing on their laptop or in a fresh clone. Doctor reports host.pointers FAIL 'run init' (Level 0 drift). The user runs `npx cookwright init`, which removes their link and writes cookwright's. Their own link text is lost, and `git status` shows the change to a committed file.
issues.evidence: Resolved by dispositions 5 and 14 (revised) and the §4.4 table. Ours means the node_modules/cookwright shape plus POINTER_TEXTS_PAST (empty), and 'any other link, dangling or resolving' is skipped, WARN naming it, never replaced. §6 tests 'a user's dangling link of another shape -> skipped, byte-identical'.

issues.problem: The pointers accept a package hoisted to the top (<top>/node_modules/cookwright). The hook commands do not: they `cd` into the config root, then test `[ -f node_modules/cookwright/bin/cookwright.mjs ]` there. The git shims do the same (shims.mjs:24,53-59). §9 nonetheless narrows B-002 to 'a package installed elsewhere than the config root or the top', which is wider than the design.
issues.suggested_fix: Either have the hook commands and shims check both places in the same order as installedPackage (config root, then top), with a test for the hoisted case, or narrow §9 honestly: B-002 keeps 'a package hoisted to the top while the config root is nested' alongside the worktree case.
issues.failure_scenario: In a monorepo, cookwright.json is at apps/mobile and npm workspaces hoist cookwright to <top>/node_modules. init writes pointers into ../../node_modules/cookwright/... that resolve, and doctor's host.pointers is PASS. But the SessionStart hook prints 'package not installed (npm install)' every session, and the pre-commit/pre-push shims print the not-installed line and check nothing, so secrets and doc sync go unscanned. B-002 has been marked narrowed past this case.
issues.evidence: Resolved by the honest-narrowing option: dispositions 6 and 16, §3 Out ('the hook commands and shims for a nested config root (B-002, as is)'), §9 (B-002 text gains 'the pointers handle a package hoisted to the top, the hooks and shims do not') and §9(f), which opens the hoisted hooks and shims.

issues.location: §4.4 'Hook commands become a function of the config root's place' and 'Pointers live at the work tree's top'
issues.problem: For a nested config root, the plan puts the pointers at the top and leaves the host settings files where init writes them today. claudeHookStep and doctor's checkClaudeHook both use path.join(repo.root, '.claude/settings.json'), which is the config root, and the Codex hostfile generalises the same logic. The new command `cd "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}/<rel>"` is correct only if a session whose project dir is the top loads <config root>/.claude/settings.json. If the session starts at the config root, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is already the config root and the cd doubles the path. Where each host loads its settings or hooks file from is neither stated nor measured, and the tests compare strings only. The claim that this closes the hook half of B-002 for nested roots is unmeasured (rule 3).
issues.suggested_fix: State where each host reads its project settings file (.claude/settings.json, .codex/hooks.json) for a session started at the top and one started in the config root. Measure it in s3/s4's scratch repo with a nested root (one session each, hook output observed). Write the settings file where the session that gets the `<rel>` form reads it, which is probably the top beside the pointers, using placement().up as the git shims do. Until then, do not claim B-002's hook half closed.
issues.failure_scenario: Config root apps/mobile, settings written at apps/mobile/.claude/settings.json with `cd "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}/apps/mobile"`. Case 1: the developer opens Claude Code in apps/mobile, so CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=<top>/apps/mobile and the cd to <top>/apps/mobile/apps/mobile fails. The ';'-joined line continues in whatever cwd the hook has, and prints a cd error plus a misleading line. Case 2: the developer opens it at the top, so Claude reads <top>/.claude/settings.json (absent) and the hook never fires. Doctor's host.hook PASSes in both cases, because it only compares the text.
issues.evidence: Resolved by disposition 16 and §4.4: the <rel> hook command is withdrawn ('Claude's hook command and the git shims are unchanged'), the B-002 hook-half claim is withdrawn, and §9(f) backlogs the work 'with the settings-file placement per host measured first'.

issues.location: §2 dispositions 10-11, §4.4 doctor (Level 0 requires host.pointers covering every shipped skill and workflow)
issues.problem: host.pointers is required at Level 0 and judges every skill and workflow the package ships. That includes `bundle`, `bundle-phase.js` and `docs-audit.js`, which disposition 11 itself flags as Level 2, experimental. A Level 0 user who does not want the experimental runner and deletes its pointer gets Level 0 drift (FAIL 'run init'), and init writes the pointer back. The only way out is to fake a 'chosen state' with a real directory. This contradicts AGENTS.md 'Every piece is optional' and the charter's levels (Level 2 installable, not required).
issues.suggested_fix: At Level 0, judge only the Level 0 skills (setup) as required. Report a missing pointer to a Level 1/2 piece as WARN, or SKIP 'not required at level 0', or judge it at its own level. SKILLS in hosts.mjs already says which skill needs workflows; give it the level too. Add a doctor test: bundle pointer deleted at Level 0, level still complete.
issues.failure_scenario: A solo developer at Level 0 removes .claude/skills/bundle and .claude/workflows/bundle-phase.js so the experimental runner never appears. Every session start shows host.pointers FAIL and 'level 0 declared: drift' with 'run init'. Running init restores the files they removed, so they cannot opt out without cheating the check (rule 2: a FAIL the user cannot clear is a bug).
issues.evidence: Resolved by dispositions 10 and 20 and §4.4. A missing pointer is FAIL only when its level is at or below the declared level, otherwise WARN '<name> (Level 2) not required at level 0'. SKILLS carries levels. §6 tests 'the bundle pointer missing at level 0 -> WARN, level complete'. The opt-out lever is backlogged in §9(e).

issues.location: §4.1 'bundle status prints scriptPath as the pointer path ... the route the kickoff precondition measured'
issues.problem: The kickoff precondition (state decision, kickoff 2026-10-16) measured `Workflow({ name: 'zzz-flow' })` resolving a named workflow through a .claude/workflows symlink. It did not measure `Workflow({ scriptPath: '.claude/workflows/<name>.js' })` through a symlink whose real path is under node_modules (or outside the repo, for an `npm install <dir>` link). The plan calls the scriptPath form measured, a claim wider than what was tested (rule 3).
issues.suggested_fix: Either print the measured form, `Workflow({ name: 'bundle-phase', args })`, or add the scriptPath-through-link run to s1's or s3's measurement. In either case, have status check that the pointer exists and say 'run init' when it does not, rather than print a path to nothing.
issues.failure_scenario: A user upgraded from stage 2 who has not run init yet calls `bundle status`, which prints `Workflow({ scriptPath: '.claude/workflows/bundle-phase.js' ... })`. That file does not exist yet, so the Workflow call fails with a not-found error rather than a cookwright line. Separately, a link whose real path is outside the session's readable tree may be refused by the runtime, and nothing measured covers that.
issues.evidence: Resolved by disposition 23, §1 ('The scriptPath form through a link was not measured; §4.1 prints the named form'), §4.1 (status prints Workflow({ name: 'bundle-phase', args }) and 'run init: the workflow pointer ... is missing') and the §6 bundle tests for both.

issues.problem: `npm install <directory>` installs node_modules/cookwright as a symlink to the checkout, outside the user repo. That is not the shape a registry install produces (a real directory). The s3/s4 measurement and the QA leg therefore test a different shape from the one shipped. §4.7 already uses the `npm pack` tarball. The plan itself notes that a Workflow script must be readable by the session ('anything under the working directory is'), and through a directory link the real path is outside the working directory.
issues.suggested_fix: Use `npm pack` and `npm install --save-dev <tarball>` for the s3/s4 scratch repo and the QA leg, as fixture.sh does, so every measurement runs against the published shape.
issues.failure_scenario: The QA leg passes on the personal app through a directory link. After `npm publish`, users get a real directory, a different shape: a difference such as a skill listed only because the realpath lands in an already-trusted checkout goes unnoticed. The reverse can also happen: the link form fails a readability check that a real install would pass, and QA reports a false bug.
issues.evidence: Resolved by disposition 23 and §8. The scratch repo is 'installed from the npm pack tarball, the published shape' (npm install --save-dev <tarball>), and the QA leg uses 'npm install of the tarball from this checkout'.

issues.location: §4.4 Codex pointers, §2 Decision 1 precondition, §8 codex exec measurement
issues.problem: The dangling-pointer case was measured for Claude Code only. For Codex, §8 measures that `codex exec` lists setup with the package installed. Whether a dangling .agents/skills/setup link, as in a fresh clone before npm install, is skipped quietly or errors at session start is not measured. The plan nonetheless commits that link for every Codex user (rule 1: a harness problem never blocks the user).
issues.suggested_fix: Add to s4's measurement checkpoint: `codex exec` in the scratch repo with node_modules removed, recording that the session runs and what it prints about the dangling skill.
issues.failure_scenario: A Codex user clones their repo on a new machine and opens Codex before `npm install`. If Codex errors or warns loudly on the unresolvable symlinked skill folder, the harness disrupts the session before the user has done anything, and doctor's WARN 'not installed where it points' gave no warning of it.
issues.evidence: Resolved by disposition 23, §8 ('codex exec ... and again with node_modules removed, recording that the session runs and what it says about the dangling link') and §10 s4 ('with codex exec, installed and dangling').

issues.location: §3 (E-014 closed), §2 disposition 8, §8 'The developer's hands, after merge'
issues.problem: E-014 is closed although the CI workflow has never run (no remote, measured), and `ci.workflow` stays unset. The outstanding steps (first push, first CI run, setting ci.workflow) are recorded only as prose in the plan's §8, and the closeout will carry them as narrative. AGENTS.md says 'No pending or next steps narrative in an active doc. A thing to do is a backlog entry', and rule 3 says claim only what was measured.
issues.suggested_fix: Keep E-014 open, narrowed to 'first GitHub run green and ci.workflow set', or open a new backlog item for it in §9's 'opened' list, so the unverified CI has a stable id.
issues.failure_scenario: After merge, the backlog shows E-014 closed. The developer pushes, ci.yml fails on GitHub (say, git user config missing in the runner for the scratch-repo tests), and nothing in the state homes records that CI was never verified or that ci.workflow is still unset. `bundle check` keeps reporting the CI row as SKIP, and nobody owns the item.
issues.evidence: Resolved as suggested: disposition 22, §3 ('E-014 narrowed') and §9 ('Backlog, narrowed: E-014 (open: the first green GitHub run and ci.workflow set ...)'). §8 says E-014 is closed by the developer on the green run.

issues.problem: The loader accepts a version-1 file and migrates it in memory, but the editor-facing schema will say `const: 2`. Every existing user's cookwright.json then shows a schema error in the editor that the CLI does not share.
issues.suggested_fix: Let the schema accept the versions the loader accepts (`enum: [1, 2]`), with a description saying 1 is migrated in memory and `npx cookwright migrate` writes 2. Parity test: schema versions = {CONFIG_VERSION} ∪ keys of MIGRATIONS.
issues.failure_scenario: The personal app updates the package. VS Code underlines `"version": 1` in red with 'must be equal to constant 2', while doctor says WARN, and the user is left with two contradictory readings of one file.
issues.evidence: Resolved by disposition 24, §4.3 ('The schema's version is enum: [1, 2] with the description saying 1 is migrated in memory; the parity test holds schema versions = {CONFIG_VERSION} ∪ keys(MIGRATIONS)'), the §6 config test ('{2} ∪ {1}') and §10 s2.

issues.location: §2 disposition 11, §4.5 ('each SKILL.md's first line names its level', 'First line: Level 0')
issues.problem: Both hosts require a SKILL.md to open with YAML frontmatter (`---`), so the file's first line cannot be the level line. Read literally, the instruction puts text ahead of the frontmatter, and the skill then does not load.
issues.suggested_fix: Say 'the first body line after the frontmatter' (the slot the bundle SKILL.md's bold line 8 holds today). Add a test that each shipped SKILL.md starts with frontmatter holding `name` and `description`.
issues.failure_scenario: The implementer writes `Level 0.` as line 1 of skills/setup/SKILL.md, followed by the frontmatter. Neither Claude Code nor Codex parses the frontmatter, so /setup or $setup is not listed. doctor's host.pointers still PASSes, since the link resolves.
issues.evidence: Resolved by disposition 11 ('first body line after the frontmatter'), §4.5 ('First body line after the frontmatter: Level 0'), disposition 24 and §6 ('each shipped SKILL.md opens with frontmatter holding name and description'), with the test in s5.

issues.location: §4.1 'A default host without workflowsDir (Codex) -> bundle refuses'
issues.problem: The refusal keys on the default (first) host, not on whether any configured host has workflows. A config with `hosts: ["codex","claude"]` is refused with 'needs a host with workflows (claude)' even though claude is configured. §4.5 step 3 tells users to add a host by editing `hosts`, so this order arises naturally.
issues.suggested_fix: Pick the first configured host that has workflowsDir for workflowScript, and refuse only when none has one. Test with [codex, claude].
issues.failure_scenario: A Codex-first developer adds claude with `hosts: ["codex","claude"]` and runs `npx cookwright bundle status x`. It exits 2 with 'the bundle runner needs a host with workflows (claude); hosts is [codex, claude]', a refusal that contradicts itself.
issues.evidence: Resolved by disposition 24 and §4.1 ('workflowScript picks the first configured host with workflowsDir; none -> bundle refuses ... hosts is [codex]'), with §6 bundle tests for hosts ['codex'] -> refusal and ['codex','claude'] -> claude's workflows.

issues.problem: The QA leg says 'the exact two lines expected', then lists three (config WARN, rules.block FAIL, host.pointers FAIL). The developer's script for the QA leg is self-contradictory.
issues.suggested_fix: Change it to 'the exact three lines expected', and say whether every other check is expected to PASS.
issues.failure_scenario: During QA the developer sees three non-PASS lines where the plan says two, and has to decide whether the extra line is a bug. That ambiguity ends up recorded as a QA finding or ignored.
issues.evidence: Resolved by disposition 24 and the §8 QA leg: 'the session's doctor line shows the three expected lines (config WARN migrated in memory, rules.block FAIL stale, host.pointers FAIL missing; every other check PASS as before)'.
